title: The derived extension-of-coefficients functor and its associativity
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C$ unital maps of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. Let $T$ be any scheme. Use the small pro-étale site and ordinary derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with constant rings $A_T,B_T,C_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Constructible means the intrinsic finite-stratification condition of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], for these arbitrary finite rings. Write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ for the full subcategory of complexes with finitely many nonzero constructible cohomology sheaves and finite Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. K-flatness and the underlying derived tensor use [def-weil-derived-tensor]; extension with its target-ring action is [def-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-scalar-extension].

1. The functor $(-)_B=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_T}B_T:D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A)\to D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$ is computed by a K-flat representative, with $B_T$ acting through the right factor. It sends $u$ to $u_B=u\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathrm{id}_{B_T}$ and is exact as a functor of triangulated categories.
2. If $K\in\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ for integers $a\leq b$, then $K_B\in\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$ has Tor amplitude in the same $[a,b]$. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.
3. If $L$ is a locally free $A_T$-module of rank one (locally isomorphic to $A_T$), then $L_B$ is the ordinary tensor $L\otimes_{A_T}B_T$, locally free of rank one over $B_T$. For the Tate example assume additionally that $\ell$ is invertible on $T$. For a common $m\geq1$ with $\ell^mA=\ell^mB=0$, use the roots-of-unity sheaf [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf] to put $A_T(1)=\mu_{\ell^m,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^m)_T}A_T$ and similarly for $B$. Define integer twists by positive tensor powers [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the unit in degree zero, and duals $M^\vee=\mathcal{H}om_{A_T}(M,A_T)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] of positive powers for negative integers. These are independent of sufficiently large $m$ and invertible by [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free], and $(A_T(r))_B\simeq B_T(r)$ canonically for every $r\in\mathbf Z$.
4. For the specified maps $f,g$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism $\alpha_K:(K_B)_C\xrightarrow{\sim}K_C$, where direct extension uses $g\circ f$. For $u:K\to L$ it satisfies $\alpha_L\circ(u_B)_C=u_C\circ\alpha_K$. If $g=\mathrm{id}_B$, $\alpha$ is the canonical tensor unitor, hence the identity after identifying extension along the identity with the identity functor. These comparisons satisfy the associativity coherence diagram for every chain $A\to B\to C\to D$ (equivalently the rebracketing pentagon, with the usual unit identifications).

proof.text: Use the published reductionDerivedExistence and its universal counit. Naturality on cochain representatives is the naturality equation of the quotient-factorized counit. K-flat invertibility is scalarCounit_isIso.

Compare the stated Tor test with the native derived tensor test through QObjTensorSingleFunctorObjIso and a K-flat resolution. The native bounded flat-model theorem gives a representative supported in [a,b]. Ordinary coefficient extension preserves flatness and K-flatness, hence preserves this representative and the same Tor interval. Its support gives bounded cohomology.

Use the proved common_stratification helper for the finitely many nonzero input cohomology sheaves. Uniqueness of universal left derived functors compares the published scalar functor with the cochain-model scalar functor. On every stratum restrictedScalarCohomology_finiteLocalModels gives finite constant B-module models. ConstantScalarComparison and finiteLocal_iff turn these into the intrinsic locally constant and finite geometric-stalk predicates.

source.place: (2), common strata and finite B-cohomology models

proof.text: Tensoring with a rank-one sheaf is an equivalence, with inverse tensoring with its dual, so it is exact. The single-complex tensor comparison makes its degree-zero complex K-flat. ScalarExtensionDual_localIsomorphism shows ordinary extension remains rank one. Apply primitive-root local models and signedLineTensor_equivalence to all Tate lines.

For degree one use the proved normalized scalar tensor tower and composition of constant coefficient ring maps. Construct positive coefficient powers recursively from scalarTensorBinaryIso and the degree-one isomorphism, using the first and second tensor-map formulas. For negative powers scalarExtensionDual_localIsomorphism makes the dual map invertible; compose it with precomposition by the inverse positive comparison. The proved dual evaluation formula cancels that inverse. Pure-tensor generation proves positive uniqueness and evaluation after the positive comparison proves negative uniqueness. Compare explicit extension with ordinary extension by ScalarHomOrdinary.extensionIso. The finite Kummer clause of tateTwist_locallyFree supplies the level-one isomorphism; tensor powers and inverse duals give the signed level family. The coefficient/exponent square holds on roots and positive tensors; both negative paths have equal evaluations on the positive comparison, and pure tensors give the ordinary square.

source.place: (3), signed Tate maps and exponent compatibility

proof.text: Use the published normalized derivedReductionComposition. Its naturality is automatic. Uniqueness of this comparison identifies the identity coefficient extension with the normalized ordinary tensor unitor from FieldStageOrdinaryRealization. Associativity is checked on cochain pure tensors and then descended by derived_natTrans_ext, using flat-term K-flat resolutions and cancellation of invertible counits.

source.place: (4), natural composition, unitor and associativity coherence

unit_route_error.failed_inference: The blueprint takes a bounded flat constructible model for arbitrary finite A and arbitrary T from lem-sf-flat-model. The current cited statement requires A=A_{E,n} and ell invertible on T; its constructible variant additionally requires a Noetherian scheme on the etale site. These hypotheses are absent here. For example A=F_ell[x,y]/(x,y)^2 has a two-dimensional cotangent space at its maximal ideal and cannot be a quotient of a discrete valuation ring by a uniformizer power; T=Spec(F_ell) also violates invertibility. The other unit sk-prop-scalar-six supplies no stated bridge from its condensed coefficients and standing schemes to these arbitrary constant-ring module categories.
unit_route_error.repair_in_proof: Steps 1--3 use generic ringed-site K-flat resolutions and the restricted-module Tor test; steps 4--5 prove intrinsic constructibility on the given finite stratification using Stacks 094H. This retains the unit statement for arbitrary finite rings and arbitrary schemes.

unit_route_error.current_flat_model_complement: The current sk-lem-sf-flat-model also contains a complement for arbitrary finite coefficient rings on a Noetherian scheme, on either small site. This is broader than lem-sf-flat-model but still does not cover the item: T=Spec(F_ell[t_1,t_2,...]) is allowed here and is not Noetherian, since the chain (t_1) subset (t_1,t_2) subset ... is strictly increasing. Its characteristic also violates the invertibility hypothesis of lem-sf-flat-model. Thus neither the original finite-type-over-the-standing-field clause nor the Noetherian complement proves the arbitrary-scheme assertion.
